title: Python complexity scoring + unresolved-ref effect fallback
description:
Two independent extensions that can be done in one session:

1. Add Python branches to complexity scoring (walk_cyclomatic, classify_cognitive, is_logical_operator)
2. Add name-only fallback for unresolved call refs in enrich_with_effects (cross-cutting — benefits Python and retroactively improves C)

Covers plan Steps 4-5 from sutra/116.

acceptance_criteria.text: is_logical_operator extended: returns true for Python boolean_operator nodes (and/or)

walk_cyclomatic has 'python' arm: if/for/while/conditional_expression/except_clause +1, boolean_operator via is_logical_operator +1, comprehensions (list/dict/set/generator) +1; try_statement and with_statement NOT counted

classify_cognitive has 'python' arm: if/conditional_expression (true,true), for/while (true,true), try_statement (true,true), except_clause (true,false), lambda (false,true), comprehensions (true,false); with_statement NOT counted

enrich_with_effects has unresolved-ref fallback: for call refs where target_symbol_id is None, match ref name against effect pattern prefixes using . as boundary; dedup against already-tagged attributes

Tests: cyclomatic count for Python function with if/for/except/and/or/comprehension; cognitive score for nested Python constructs; effect enrichment fires for unresolved 'open', 'requests.get', 'subprocess.run' patterns

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (covers sutra/188 + sutra/189 together):

Verdict: needs-attention

Findings:
1. [high] Unresolved Python effect fallback does not see real dotted calls (attributes.rs:155-162) — Python parser records identifier refs only; for `requests.get()`, the call ref is the attribute identifier `get`, not `requests`. Because `enrich_all_effects` passes only `context_kind == "call"` refs, dotted prefixes like `requests` or `subprocess` won't match. Tests synthesize dotted RefRows so they pass but don't cover the production parser path.
2. [high] Greedy prefix resolution can turn invalid imports into local edges (python_imports.rs:160-175) — `try_resolve_segments` walks shorter prefixes until any module/package exists. `import pkg.foo.bar` resolves to `pkg/foo.py` when it exists, even though Python requires `pkg.foo` to be a package.
3. [medium] Auto-discovered package roots resolve duplicates nondeterministically (python_imports.rs:71-106) — HashSet iteration order means same import can resolve to different files across runs in monorepos with multiple roots containing the same package name.
